findings.where: Left cabinet's right side face x 737-758, y 860-1300; right cabinet's left side face x 1647-1666, y 860-1310
findings.what: The visible side face of each Tropos cabinet reads white or gray, not red. Left cabinet's right side measures L* 70-74, C* 13. Right cabinet's left side measures L* 57-61, C* 3-4. In the studio reference the side face is dark red (L* 10.6, C* 34.8). Seen at web size beside the reference, the left Tropos looks like a white box with a pink-red film on the front, not a cabinet of acrylic tinted right through. The only red on the side is the small dark-red handle slot. The 256-sample frame looks the same, so the join did not cause this.
findings.expected: Side faces in the same red as the front and horn, as in the approved studio front. Any glancing reflection of the wall should sit on top of visible red, not replace it.

findings.where: C: ball x 568-877, y 948-1240 (base x 580-870, y 1220-1355). A: Core on the credenza, about x 1394-1468, y 880-975
findings.what: The Core ball reads as a dark brown mirror ball, like a smoked gazing ball or a Christmas ornament, not as Ember-red acrylic with an opal diffuser inside. Its body measures L* 19, C* 17, hue 46 degrees (brown). The studio Core off measures L* 46, C* 92, hue 39 degrees. The ball sits in front of a bright window, yet it does not glow red the way tinted acrylic with an opal core does when lit from behind. All you see is a mirror image of the room on a dark brown body. Only the frosted base reads red (sunlit side L* 36, C* 41). The Core in A reads the same at its small size (ball C* 16, hue 46 degrees; base L* 8).
findings.expected: A ball that reads as the same bright, deep red as core-ember-off.png, with the window reflections on top of it.

findings.what: Below a fuzzy fabric roll, the upholstered, bulging sofa back carries a crisp oak cathedral grain that looks like the floor's wood texture. It runs horizontally and has a pale piping line across it. The arm blocks at bottom right carry the same grain. At web size the foreground reads as a curved wooden barrel, not the back of a fabric sofa, and it fills the bottom sixth of the frame.
findings.expected: Upholstery fabric (weave or bouclé) on the sofa back and arm, with soft fabric shading.

findings.where: Left cabinet front x 462-735, y 870-1290 vs horn x 470-760, y 690-830 (right pair the same)
findings.what: Answering the chroma question: the fronts still read as red, but not the same red as the horn above them. The horns measure hue 38-39 degrees at C* 57-61 (orange-red). The lighter parts of the front, where the pale lining shows through, measure hue 14-17 degrees at C* 27 (pink), and the upper front measures hue 31 degrees at C* 42. In the studio, front and horn are both about 39-40 degrees. At web size each speaker looks two-tone: a saturated orange-red horn on a paler, pinker, milky cabinet. The white sides (A1) make this worse.
findings.expected: Front and horn reading as one material and one hue family, as in front-ember.png. This concerns hue as well as chroma.

findings.what: The rug is a perfectly even gray field with a darker gray border band. Channel standard deviation is about 2.4 levels over a 200x80 px patch. Fine texture (high-pass std) is 0.89, below the painted wall (1.29) and the oak floor (1.91). It shows no pile, no fiber, no light falloff and no thickness or shadow where it meets the oak. The border meets the floor as a knife-sharp straight line. It reads like a gray mat painted on the floor.
findings.expected: Visible weave or pile texture, slight tonal variation from the window light, and a small edge thickness or contact shadow.

findings.what: Both Tropos power cords stop in mid-air about 14 px below a blank white wall plate. The plates have no receptacles and no plug sits in them, so the cord ends as a cut tube. At full size it is plain. At web size the right one shows as a black cord hanging from just under a white rectangle.
findings.expected: A duplex receptacle with a plug in it and the cord leaving the plug, or the cord running behind the cabinet with no visible end.

findings.where: C: book x ~1100-1320, y ~1215-1470 (partly behind the glass). A: book on the side table, about x 250-320, y 960-1000
findings.what: The book shows no page block. Both visible edges are solid color: the long front edge is a flat gray-green and the short right edge is flat gray. There are no paper lines, no cream page edge and no board overhang. It reads as a gray-green box or slab, not a closed book, and at 700 px it is one of the largest props beside the lamp. The cover's top surface is sunlit and nearly white, with a smooth curved shadow across it.
findings.expected: At least one visible edge showing cream page edges recessed between the boards, as any closed book does from this angle.

findings.what: The faceted tumbler is correctly soft (it sits in front of the focus plane). It shows refraction, and the red lamp appears flipped on its right side. But I find no water line, meniscus or bright surface ellipse. The top shows the faceted inner wall fanning down, which is what an empty glass shows. As drawn, it reads as an empty crystal tumbler, not a glass of water.
findings.expected: If water is intended, a visible water level a little below the rim, with its bright or dark surface band.

findings.where: Right box left feather x 1650-1666, y 640-1319
findings.what: The joins are clean: I see no seam along any edge of either box at full size with the contrast raised, and the edges match the 256-sample frame. One note: the right box's left feather runs through the right cabinet's left side face (x 1647-1666) and the right horn's left rim (about x 1665). Those pixels are a 256/1024 blend, and the leftmost 3 px of the cabinet come from the 256 frame. At 4x I see no doubling there. If the box is re-cut, start it about 30 px further left.
findings.expected: Feather entirely in plain wall or floor.

(1) Both Tropos show white or gray side faces (L* 57-74, C* 3-13; the studio side is dark red), so the left one reads as a white box with a pink front. (2) The foreground sofa back carries oak wood grain where its fabric should be. To fix before final: front and horn read as two different reds (pink vs orange-red), the gray rug is flat, and both power cords end in mid-air under blank wall plates.

The rest is photographic: depth of field is consistent (near table corner soft, glass soft, lamp sharp, background soft), verticals are straight, and the sun on the table and shelf is believable.

findings.what: The Core, the only product in C, reads as a dark maroon-brown mirror ball, not the bright red Ember Core. Across the ball the median is L* 22.5, C* 16.8, h 40. Only 8% of the ball reads red (C* over 40) and 43% is darker than L* 20. The studio off frame gives L* 44.5 and C* 75, with 95% of the ball red and 80% bright red. The opal diffuser does not show at all. Because the body is so dark, the room's mirror reflection takes over the whole ball, so it looks like a dark glass ornament. The base reads near-white pink where the sun hits it (L* 83, C* 13, rgb 236,200,196) and brown in shade (L* 34, C* 20). The studio base reads L* 51 / C* 81 lit and L* 40 / C* 73 in shade.
findings.expected: The ball should read solid, saturated red like core-ember-off.png, with most of it above C* 40 and about L* 40-45 on the lit half, the opal giving it body. The base should read red, with a dark rim only at the foot.

findings.what: The Core on the credenza reads as a dark brown, nearly black ball with a thin red rim. Across the ball the median is L* 17.1, C* 14.2. Only 3% of the ball reads red and 63% is darker than L* 20. The base reads L* 15-22, C* 9-18 (dark brown). At 1300 px wide it is a ball about 40 px across that a visitor would take for brown or black glass.
findings.expected: It should read as the same saturated red ball as the studio Core off (95% of the ball red, median C* 75).

found.q1_A_ready: No. Even setting the Mantle region aside, two blocking problems remain. First, the Core on the credenza reads as a dark brown, nearly black ball: only 3% of it reads red, against 95% in the studio. Second, both Tropos cabinets have white or neutral-grey sides and tops (C* 2.8 and 13, against 35 in the studio), so they read as red fronts on white boxes. The horns read as Ember. About 45% of each cabinet front reads rose/pink rather than the studio's deep red (fix). Both power cords stop below blank wall plates (fix), and the ports look crumpled at full size (fix). The scale is right. When the Mantle is re-rendered, its plinth also has to read red: today it measures C* 6.
found.q2_C_ready: No. The Core is the only product in C, and it does not read as Ember off. It reads as a dark maroon-brown mirror ball: across the ball L* 22.5 and C* 16.8, with 8% red, against L* 44.5, C* 75 and 95% red in the studio. The opal does not show. Everything else holds: there is no dock or cable, the ball looks the right size beside the glass and the book, and the room's reflection in it is believable.
found.q3_reads_wrong: In A: a buyer would see the Tropos as a cabinet with a red front and white sides, a pinker red than the studio and than its own horn, with power cords that stop short of the wall plates. The Core would look like a dark brown or black glass ball, not an Ember lamp. The Mantle would look like a grey and black turntable. In C: the Core would look like a dark oxblood or brown mirrored glass ball on a pinkish-mauve base. A buyer expecting the bright red ball shown in the studio pictures would think C shows a different color, or a different, darker product.
